Design spec, 2026-09-28 (v3). Nothing is built yet; every flow below is the plan. Backend and database scope is locked to the Semester 3 handbook (AY 2026-27): CSA213 Advanced Programming and CSA214 Data Engineering. Frontend uses the React covered in detail last semester. Every diagram is pre-drawn, so it shows the same everywhere. Use Full size on any diagram to see it at 100% and scroll sideways.

Velora — System Flowcharts

Emergency medicine discovery and admin-attested 24/7 pharmacy access. A patient searches a medicine, sees which nearby verified pharmacies are open and have it in stock, and can hold one unit for 30 minutes before travelling.

One Express + TypeScript API · Prisma ORM on PostgreSQL as the only source of truth · MongoDB as a copy used for fast search · JWT + refresh tokens + RBAC · React 18 SPA with React Router and TanStack Query. No Redis, no queue, no PostGIS, no microservices: none of them are in the syllabus.

CSA213: Node, Express, Prisma, JWT, RBAC, TS CSA214: PostgreSQL, SQL, normalisation, indexing, MongoDB Frontend: React 18 + Vite + TS Postgres decides, Mongo copies Search needs no login Hold = one transaction Verification is admin-attested REST /api/v1 · 30 endpoints 9 tables · 2 collections Roles: PATIENT · PHARMACIST · ADMIN Hold lasts 30 min
Colour key Client / React Express routes, middleware, checks Services, hooks, Prisma Databases Success Error / rejected Outside Velora Note Sequence diagrams read top to bottom; circles are step numbers; a dotted alt box shows the possible outcomes.

01 System Architecture CSA213CSA214

Who uses Velora, what sits outside it, and the three layers inside it.

Why two databases: CSA214 teaches both, and each has a real job here. PostgreSQL holds relations, constraints and transactions. MongoDB holds one ready-made document per stock item, shaped for the search screen. A hold is never confirmed from MongoDB.

03 Request Path + MVC Structure CSA213 wk 3–7

First the app-level middleware every request passes through, in the order it is registered in app.ts. Then one real request, placing a hold, followed through the folders it touches.

// src/app.ts
const app = express();
app.use(express.json());          // built-in
app.use(cookieParser());          // third-party
app.use(morgan('dev'));           // third-party logging

app.use('/api/v1/auth',       authRoutes);
app.use('/api/v1/search',     searchRoutes);
app.use('/api/v1/holds',      holdRoutes);
app.use('/api/v1/pharmacies', pharmacyRoutes);
app.use('/api/v1/admin',      adminRoutes);

app.use(notFound);                // 404 for unknown paths
app.use(errorHandler);            // must be last
export default app;

// src/routes/holds.routes.ts
router.post('/', authenticate, authorize('PATIENT'),
            validate(placeHoldSchema), asyncHandler(holdController.create));
velora/
├─ client/                  React SPA (§13)
└─ server/
   ├─ prisma/
   │  ├─ schema.prisma      models, relations, @@index
   │  ├─ migrations/
   │  └─ seed.ts
   ├─ data/                 medicines, pharmacies, areas .json
   └─ src/
      ├─ server.ts          app.listen(process.env.PORT)
      ├─ app.ts
      ├─ routes/            auth search holds pharmacies admin
      ├─ controllers/       one per route file
      ├─ services/          AuthService SearchService HoldService
      │                     StockService PharmacyService AdminService
      ├─ middlewares/       authenticate authorize validate
      │                     notFound errorHandler
      ├─ validators/        request schemas per route
      ├─ db/                prisma.ts, mongo.ts
      ├─ types/             express.d.ts adds req.user
      └─ utils/             AppError.ts asyncHandler.ts jwt.ts
  1. routes/ only lists the endpoint and its middleware. No logic.
  2. controllers/ reads req, calls one service method, sends res. Never imports Prisma.
  3. services/ are TypeScript classes holding the business rules; they run every database call and every transaction.
  4. errorHandler turns any thrown AppError into a clean JSON error (§12).

04 Authentication + RBAC CSA213 wk 8–9

A short-lived access JWT kept in the React app's memory, plus a 7-day refresh token sent as an httpOnly cookie and stored hashed in PostgreSQL. Registration offers PATIENT or PHARMACIST; the one ADMIN account comes from the seed script.

Route groupWhoExtra check in the service
GET /searchanyone—
/holdsPATIENTonly their own holds
/pharmacies/:id/*PHARMACISTmust own pharmacy :id; a role alone doesn't prove that
/admin/*ADMINevery decision writes an audit_log row
 
// access token payload, signed with JWT_ACCESS_SECRET
{ "sub": 12, "role": "PHARMACIST", "iat": 1790580000, "exp": 1790580900 }

// refresh cookie set on login and refresh
res.cookie('refreshToken', token, {
  httpOnly: true,               // JavaScript can't read it
  secure: isProd,
  sameSite: 'lax',
  path: '/api/v1/auth',         // only sent to auth routes
  maxAge: 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000,
});

// middlewares/authorize.ts
export const authorize = (...roles: Role[]) =>
  (req, _res, next) =>
    roles.includes(req.user.role) ? next()
      : next(new AppError(403, 'Forbidden'));

Why a cookie for the refresh token: localStorage can be read by any script on the page, an httpOnly cookie can't. The frontend and API share one origin through a Vercel rewrite (§15), so the cookie stays first-party and needs no CORS setup.

05 Emergency Search CSA214 wk 3–7, 12

The most important read path, with no login in the way. MongoDB finds candidates quickly; PostgreSQL then confirms each pharmacy is verified and open right now, and sorts them by distance using plain SQL.

  1. Steps 1–2: the page sends the medicine name and the patient's location. No token is needed.
  2. Steps 3–4: MongoDB returns up to 50 pharmacies whose copy says the medicine is in stock (§10).
  3. Steps 5–6: PostgreSQL keeps only VERIFIED pharmacies that are open now, measures the distance, and sorts nearest first.
  4. Steps 7–11: the badge says CONFIRMED if stock was updated in the last 6 hours, otherwise STALE. If nothing is found, same-salt alternatives are offered.
-- SearchService: $1 ids from Mongo, $2 lat, $3 lng,
-- $4 dLat, $5 dLng, $6 radiusKm, $7 medicine id
WITH nearby AS (
  SELECT v.id, v.name, v.phone, v.lat, v.lng,
         6371 * 2 * ASIN(SQRT(
           POWER(SIN(RADIANS(v.lat - $2) / 2), 2) +
           COS(RADIANS($2)) * COS(RADIANS(v.lat)) *
           POWER(SIN(RADIANS(v.lng - $3) / 2), 2)
         )) AS distance_km
  FROM verified_open_pharmacy v          -- view, §08
  WHERE v.id = ANY($1)
    AND v.lat BETWEEN $2 - $4 AND $2 + $4
    AND v.lng BETWEEN $3 - $5 AND $3 + $5
)
SELECT n.*, s.quantity, s.price,
       CASE WHEN s.last_updated >= NOW() - INTERVAL '6 hours'
            THEN 'CONFIRMED' ELSE 'STALE' END AS stock_badge
FROM nearby n
JOIN stock_item s ON s.pharmacy_id = n.id AND s.medicine_id = $7
WHERE n.distance_km <= $6 AND s.quantity > 0
ORDER BY n.distance_km
LIMIT 20;

-- no results: self join for the same salt
SELECT m2.id, m2.name
FROM medicine m1
JOIN medicine m2 ON m2.composition = m1.composition
                AND m2.id <> m1.id
WHERE m1.id = $7;

The final s.quantity > 0 check runs against PostgreSQL, so a stale "in stock" in MongoDB can never show a pharmacy that is actually sold out.

06 Stock Hold: One ACID Transaction CSA213 wk 7CSA214 wk 8correctness-critical

Two patients tap "Hold" on the last unit at the same moment. Only one may win. The quantity is lowered by one only if it is still at least one, inside a Prisma transaction, so the database decides the winner.

// services/HoldService.ts
async placeHold(patientId: number, stockItemId: number) {
  const active = await prisma.hold.count({ where: { patientId, status: 'ACTIVE' } });
  if (active > 0) throw new AppError(409, 'You already have an active hold');

  const hold = await prisma.$transaction(async (tx) => {
    // 1. lazy expiry: release this item's old holds and give the units back
    const expired = await tx.hold.updateMany({
      where: { stockItemId, status: 'ACTIVE', expiresAt: { lt: new Date() } },
      data:  { status: 'EXPIRED' },
    });
    if (expired.count > 0) {
      await tx.stockItem.update({
        where: { id: stockItemId },
        data:  { quantity: { increment: expired.count } },
      });
    }
    // 2. lower quantity by 1, but only if at least 1 is left
    const res = await tx.stockItem.updateMany({
      where: { id: stockItemId, quantity: { gte: 1 } },
      data:  { quantity: { decrement: 1 } },
    });
    if (res.count === 0) throw new AppError(409, 'Just missed it');   // rolls back

    // 3. record the hold
    return tx.hold.create({
      data: { stockItemId, patientId, status: 'ACTIVE',
              expiresAt: new Date(Date.now() + 30 * 60_000) },
    });
  });

  await this.mongo.availability.updateOne({ _id: stockItemId }, { $inc: { quantity: -1 } });
  return hold;
}

Why the conditional update works: UPDATE ... WHERE quantity >= 1 takes a row lock, so the second transaction waits, then re-checks the condition against the committed value and updates 0 rows. That is the Isolation part of ACID doing the work.

07 Stock, Opening Hours, Seed Data CSA213 wk 2, 6–7CSA214 wk 10

Pharmacists keep their own stock and hours up to date; a seed script provides demo data. PostgreSQL saves first, then MongoDB's copy is updated. If the copy fails, the row is flagged so an admin can repair search, instead of it silently going wrong.

08 Pharmacy Approval + Compliance Queries CSA214 wk 4, 6–7admin-attested

No Indian pharmacy council offers a public licence-check API, so an admin checks each licence by hand. Only VERIFIED pharmacies appear in search, and every admin decision writes an audit_log row in the same transaction.

Compliance dashboard

Question the admin asksSQL techniqueWk
Which licences expire in the next 30 days with no newer licence on file?CTE + correlated NOT EXISTS7
Has this pharmacy been suspended before?correlated EXISTS on audit_log7
Which verified pharmacies are missing hours for some day?CROSS JOIN days 0–6, LEFT JOIN hours, keep NULLs6
Which pharmacies let more than 5 holds expire this week?GROUP BY + HAVING + date functions4
Which pharmacies are open right now?VIEW with a non-equi join on hours6–7
Which pharmacies stock nothing at all?non-correlated subquery with NOT IN6
 
-- wk 7: CTE + correlated NOT EXISTS
WITH expiring AS (
  SELECT c.pharmacy_id, c.license_number, c.expiry_date
  FROM credential c
  WHERE c.expiry_date BETWEEN CURRENT_DATE
                          AND CURRENT_DATE + INTERVAL '30 days'
)
SELECT p.name, e.license_number, e.expiry_date
FROM expiring e
JOIN pharmacy p ON p.id = e.pharmacy_id
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM credential c2
  WHERE c2.pharmacy_id = e.pharmacy_id
    AND c2.expiry_date > e.expiry_date
);

-- wk 7: correlated EXISTS
SELECT p.id, p.name,
       EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM audit_log a
               WHERE a.pharmacy_id = p.id
                 AND a.action = 'SUSPEND') AS was_suspended
FROM pharmacy p
WHERE p.status = 'VERIFIED';
-- wk 6-7: view with a non-equi join for "open now"
CREATE VIEW verified_open_pharmacy AS
SELECT p.id, p.name, p.phone, p.lat, p.lng, p.is_24x7
FROM pharmacy p
JOIN operating_hours oh
  ON  oh.pharmacy_id = p.id
  AND oh.day_of_week = EXTRACT(DOW FROM NOW())
  AND CURRENT_TIME BETWEEN oh.open_time AND oh.close_time
WHERE p.status = 'VERIFIED';

-- wk 6: cross join to find missing days
SELECT p.name, d.day
FROM pharmacy p
CROSS JOIN generate_series(0, 6) AS d(day)
LEFT JOIN operating_hours oh
  ON oh.pharmacy_id = p.id AND oh.day_of_week = d.day
WHERE p.status = 'VERIFIED' AND oh.id IS NULL;

-- wk 4: GROUP BY + HAVING
SELECT s.pharmacy_id, COUNT(*) AS expired_holds
FROM hold h JOIN stock_item s ON s.id = h.stock_item_id
WHERE h.status = 'EXPIRED'
  AND h.expires_at >= DATE_TRUNC('week', NOW())
GROUP BY s.pharmacy_id
HAVING COUNT(*) > 5;

09 PostgreSQL Data Model CSA214 wk 1–2, 5, 8

Nine tables, normalised to BCNF. PK = primary key, FK = foreign key, UK = unique. The crow's foot end of a line is the "many" side.

FormRuleWhere Velora shows it
1NFone value per columnopening hours are one row per day, never "Mon-Sat 9-9" in a text column
2NFnothing depends on part of a composite keystock_item has UNIQUE (pharmacy_id, medicine_id); quantity and price depend on both
3NFno non-key column depends on another non-key columnlicence details live in credential, so a renewal adds a row instead of editing pharmacy
BCNFevery determinant is a candidate keycomposition and form live only in medicine, keyed by its id
 
// prisma/schema.prisma (excerpt)
model StockItem {
  id          Int      @id @default(autoincrement())
  pharmacy    Pharmacy @relation(fields: [pharmacyId], references: [id])
  pharmacyId  Int
  medicine    Medicine @relation(fields: [medicineId], references: [id])
  medicineId  Int
  quantity    Int                          // CHECK added in SQL migration
  price       Decimal  @db.Decimal(8, 2)
  lastUpdated DateTime @default(now())
  mongoSynced Boolean  @default(true)
  holds       Hold[]

  @@unique([pharmacyId, medicineId])
  @@index([medicineId, quantity])
}

enum HoldStatus { ACTIVE COLLECTED CANCELLED EXPIRED }

10 MongoDB Documents + Pipelines CSA214 wk 10–12

Two collections, both rebuilt from PostgreSQL. Medicine details are embedded because search always shows them together; pharmacies are referenced because one pharmacy appears in hundreds of documents.

ChoiceEmbed or referenceReason
medicine inside availabilityembedalways read together, medicine rarely changes
pharmacy inside availabilityreferenceone pharmacy, hundreds of docs; verified status changes
holdsnot in MongoDBholds need transactions; PostgreSQL only
 
// SearchService, step 1
db.availability.aggregate([
  { $match:  { 'medicine.name': { $regex: q, $options: 'i' },
               available: true } },
  { $lookup: { from: 'pharmacies', localField: 'pharmacyId',
               foreignField: '_id', as: 'pharmacy' } },
  { $match:  { 'pharmacy.verified': true } },
  { $sort:   { lastUpdated: -1 } },
  { $limit:  50 },
]);

11 Indexing + Query Optimisation CSA214 wk 9

Seed enough rows that a full scan is slow, measure, add an index, measure again. The before/after timings go into the project report.

IndexSpeeds up
stock_item (medicine_id, quantity)who has medicine X in stock
pharmacy (status, lat, lng)verified pharmacies inside the search box
operating_hours (pharmacy_id, day_of_week)the open-now view
credential (pharmacy_id, expiry_date)expiring-licence query
hold (stock_item_id, status, expires_at)lazy expiry inside the hold transaction
availability { 'medicine.name': 1, available: 1 }MongoDB $match stage
 
-- what to look for in the output
EXPLAIN ANALYZE SELECT ... ;
-- before: Seq Scan on stock_item  (actual time=0.02..41.8 rows=...)
-- after:  Index Scan using stock_item_medicine_id_quantity_idx
-- record "Execution Time" for each, 5 runs, take the median

12 Error Handling + Event Loop CSA213 wk 10–11

One custom error class, one async wrapper, and one error middleware registered last. Known errors get a clear message; unknown ones become a generic 500 with the stack logged on the server, never sent to the browser.

// utils/AppError.ts
export class AppError extends Error {
  constructor(public status: number, message: string,
              public details?: unknown) {
    super(message);
  }
}

// utils/asyncHandler.ts
export const asyncHandler = (fn) => (req, res, next) =>
  Promise.resolve(fn(req, res, next)).catch(next);

// error body the frontend always receives
{ "error": { "status": 409, "message": "Just missed it" } }
  1. Use bcrypt's async API, never hashSync.
  2. Use fs.promises in the seed script; never readFileSync inside a request.
  3. Paginate every list endpoint with Prisma take and skip (default 20, max 50).
  4. Let SQL filter and sort; never load a whole table and loop over it in a handler.
  5. Never await inside a loop when the calls are independent; use Promise.all.

13 Frontend Architecture React, Sem 2

A client-rendered React 18 + TypeScript SPA built with Vite. React Router handles pages, TanStack Query holds everything that came from the API, AuthContext with useReducer holds the logged-in user, and plain useState holds the rest.

ConcernChoiceDetail
BuildVite + React 18 + TypeScriptdev server proxies /api to the local API
RoutingReact Router v6 createBrowserRouternested layouts, RequireAuth and RequireRole wrappers, React.lazy for dashboards
Server stateTanStack Querysearch: stale 30 s, refetch every 60 s and on focus; mutations invalidate ['search'] and ['holds','me']
Auth stateAuthContext + useReduceractions LOGIN, TOKEN_REFRESHED, LOGOUT; access token in memory only
URL stateuseSearchParams?medicine=&area= so a search can be shared or reloaded
FormsReact Hook Form + Zodsame rules as the API; server 400 field errors mapped back onto inputs
Custom hooksuseAuth, useSearch, usePlaceHold, useGeolocation, useDebounce, useCountdowncomponents never call fetch directly
StylingTailwind CSS, mobile-first44 px minimum tap targets, text contrast at least 4.5:1
Errorsroute-level error boundary + toastsApiError status decides the message
TestingVitest + React Testing LibraryRequireRole, the refresh logic in api/client.ts, useCountdown

Location comes from the browser's location prompt. If the patient says no, they pick their area from a list of seeded areas with known coordinates. "Directions" opens a Google Maps link with the pharmacy's coordinates, so no maps API key is needed. The companion Velora Frontend page has the full frontend breakdown.
